title: Cohort-temporal smoothing rollback composer for cross-metric SLOs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver an automated rollback trigger composer that combines cohort-specific baselining and temporal smoothing to make robust, explainable rollback decisions across multiple SLO signals (p99 latency, error rate, token cost per request, and throughput).

Rationale: Existing single-threshold or static multi-threshold rollbacks are brittle across cohorts (mobile vs desktop, spike vs steady traffic) and sensitive to transient noise. This ticket designs and implements a composer that:
- Computes cohort-aware baselines and drift-aware deltas
- Applies short-term exponential smoothing + long-term trend damping to avoid oscillation
- Combines signals via a weighted ensemble where weights include cost-sensitivity and customer-impact profiles
- Adds dynamic hysteresis windows (traffic-weighted) to prevent flip-flopping during rollout phases
- Supports offline replay tuning and lightweight online Bayesian updates to thresholds

Scope: design and implement the core composer service and a simulation harness for historical replay. Integrate with existing rollout controller to emit roll, hold, or escalate decisions and surface explainability metadata to Console (per-route dashboard). Not in scope: full UI polish for Console rollout editor (separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Composer produces a single decision (ALLOW/HOLD/ROLLBACK/ESCALATE) for canary, A/B, and shadow traffic given a rollout config and live metric streams.
Decisions include explanation: cohort baseline deltas, smoothing windows used, ensemble score breakdown and the dominant signal.
False-positive rollback rate in replayed historical experiments is <= 1.5% relative to current manual thresholds across three representative services (chat, embeddings, reranking).
Composer exposes a /simulate endpoint to run offline replay with configurable noise models and outputs a scored threshold tuning recommendation JSON.

Integration tests validate decision monotonicity under traffic surge (no more than 1 decision flip per 10 minutes for the same canary cohort) and that hysteresis prevents immediate rollback after transient blips.
Performance: composer adds <10ms median latency to the decision path for synchronous canary gating and scales to 200 concurrent canary evaluations per minute per region with current Dedicated sizing.
notes: Decision model: ensemble score = sum(w_i * normalized_delta_i) where i in {latency_p99, error_rate, token_cost, throughput}. We will normalize deltas using cohort-specific MAD and apply a sigmoid transform for robustness.
Smoothing strategy: Short window EWMA alpha=0.35, long window EWMA alpha=0.05; combine with weighted average where weights are traffic-volume-normalized.

Tuning: offline replay will run thousands of simulated rollouts using historical traces (last 18 months) with injected synthetic latency spikes and traffic shifts. Use expected regret and false positive/negative rates to recommend thresholds.
Cost sensitivity: token_cost will be multiplied by a tenant-level cost_factor to bias decisions away from rollbacks for low-value cheap requests where latency regressions are acceptable.
Explainability: front-end needs breakdown per cohort; include top-2 drivers and a short natural-language summary for operators.
Fallback: if composer fails or is unhealthy, controller will fallback to the existing static-guard policy (configurable via feature flag).
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with product and SRE. Agreed on cohort dimensions: client_type (mobile/web), region, route, and API version.
2026-02-18: Prototype EWMA smoothing and ensemble scoring implemented in a local simulator. Initial replay on chat service showed 2.8% false positives; need tuning.
2026-02-24: Added cohort-specific MAD normalization which reduced false positives to 1.4% on the chat baseline. Verified stability under synthetic surge tests.

2026-03-03: PR #482 opened for rollout-controller integration. Design review notes: add traffic-weighted hysteresis and ensure the composer can operate in async (eventual) mode for low-priority canaries.
2026-03-08: SRE requested a kill-switch and healthcheck metrics: composer_decision_latency_ms, composer_error_count, composer_model_version. Implemented health endpoint and Prometheus metrics.
2026-03-10: Internal canary scheduled against a low-traffic internal tenant next week (2026-03-16). Need final sign-off from security for simulated replay data access.
